2026 Paris Motor Show • XPENG Reveals G9L at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, Dubbed As the Ultimate "Large SUV for the AI Era"
Leapmotor B05 Electric Hatchback To Be Produced in Spain at Stellantis Group's Zaragoza Plant
9 photos
Photo: Leapmotor
Now retailing at less than 20,000 euros in Spain, the B05 is good for nearly 300 miles on a full charge. Although sport utility vehicles are all the rage in the European Union and the United Kingdom right now, the full-electric hatchback from Leapmotor will soon join the B10 crossover at the Stellantis group's Zaragoza plant.
Leapmotor hasn't said when B05 production is scheduled to start in Zaragoza , how many will be produced on a yearly basis, or how many euros the project will require. For the time being, a confirmation is all that Leapmotor is willing to share with the media. A coupe-like compact that looks really nice when compared to the overly clinical Volkswagen ID.3 Neo, the newcomer is more than meets the eye.
The same can be said about Leapmotor's decision to expand production to Spain. For starters, the Chinese automaker helps the Stellantis plant bring its factory closer to Zaragoza's declared maximum yearly output. Stellantis, meanwhile, brings the infrastructure and manufacturing footprint that would otherwise take years and substantial investments if Leapmotor were to do it alone.
Chinese automakers need more than large shipping vessels and a distributor to make a difference in the European space. They need proper spare parts logistics, customer support, service facilities, and a way to build vehicles closer to the markets where Chinese brands intend to sell them. Better still, this arrangement helps Leapmotor dodge a very prohibitive European import tariff.
The joint venture with Stellantis went live in 2024, with the Franco-Italian-American partner holding 51 percent. Stellantis, therefore, controls the Chinese partner's export, sales, and manufacturing activities outside China. The joint venture had grown to more than 850 sales and service locations across Europe by May 2026, and the B05 cements said partnership.
Photo: Leapmotor Also worth noting, the commercial ambition of the Chinese party is easier to understand when you look at the B05's pricing information for the Spanish market. After including the 3,375-euro Plan Auto+ subsidy and 900 euros from energy-saving certificates, the starting price of the compact electric hatchback falls to a very reasonable 19,400 euros.
This offer applies to the entry LifePro version with the 56.2 kilowatt-hour battery. For maximum range, customers have to select the larger battery. In its case, Leapmotor claims 482 kilometers (299 miles) in the WLTP. If you feel like Stellantis got the short stick, bear in mind that its own electric vehicle push failed to compete against Chinese rivals.
Stellantis has openly stated that it wants to use Leapmotor's electric vehicle technologies and cost base to strengthen its own electrification plans, and B05 production in Spain will certainly help the group develop more affordable EVs across its core brands. Stellantis and Leapmotor laid out the former's ambition in May 2026, confirming that Stellantis could use Leapmotor International's ecosystem to improve EV production costs.
Joint purchasing will also prove useful. Combining demand gives Stellantis and Leapmotor a stronger position when negotiating supplier contracts, therefore resulting in cheaper supplied components. But wait, there's more! European supply chains can support resilience, helping the partners move new models to market a little bit faster.
Inside, the rear-drive B05 gets a large central touchscreen, 21 driver-assistance functions, seven airbags, and plenty more as standard. The higher Design grade sweetens the deal with heated front seats, a heated steering wheel, a panoramic sunroof, and 12-speaker audio as opposed to six for the Life trim level. All in all, not bad for a model that competes against the Volkswagen ID.3 Pro and Stellantis' very own Peugeot e-308 .
